newsitem.title: USA: 50-OFF files for prfrd shr offering.
newsitem.headline: 50-OFF files for prfrd shr offering.

text.p: 50-OFF Stores Inc, a bankrupt retailer, said on Monday it is proposing a preferred stock offering as part of its reorganization plan.
On April 11, 50-OFF filed a registration statement for an offering of up to 122,009 units and not less than 30,500 units at $100 per unit, the company said.

Each unit is comprised of 20 shares each of the new series A preferred stock and the new common stock that the company proposes to issue and sell upon confirmation of a reorganization plan, 50-OFF said.
Judge Lief Clark, of the the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Western District of Texas, has set a confirmation hearing date June 3, 1997, for the reorganization plan, 50-OFF said.
50-OFF said that it has issued to shareholders one right to subscribe for and purchase one unit for each share of common stock held as of March 21, 1997.
As of March 21, 1997, there were 12.2 million shares of common stock outstanding, 50-OFF said.
Each non-transferable right entitles the holder to subscribe for one unit prior to May 20, 1997, at which time the Rights expire, the company said.

Each share of the new series A preferred stock will have a $5.00 stated and liquidation value and is convertible into two shares of new Common Stock. The Stock will pay a $0.275 cumulative annual dividend.
